entities.name: Harry Cane
entities.description:
Harry Cane, also known as Billy Speed, is an Adventurers minifigure introduced in 1998. He makes appearances in the Egypt and Jungle sub-themes.

Harry Cane has black legs, and an earth orange torso printed with an aviator's jacket. His arms are earth orange, and his hands and head are bright yellow. His face has a smirking expression, a black moustache, stubble, and sideburns. He wears an earth orange aviator's helmet with black goggles.

In 5784 Soccer Mania, Billy Speed has grey pants instead of black.

Compared to other Adventurers Egypt characters, Harry Cane's name is one of the most consistent across different markets, regions, and publications. However, there are still a few instances where his name is changed.

entities.description:
3382 Jing Lee the Wanderer 4224631 Jing Lee Key Chain KC36 Jing Lee Key Chain

Jing Lee, also called the Wanderer, is an Adventurers Orient Expedition minifigure introduced in 2003.

Jing Lee has a black ponytail. Her face has short eyebrows, ovular eyes, and pale lips. She wears a green oriental shirt with black Chinese symbols (禾中, Hé Zhōng) and yellow embroidery, and red pants.

Jing Lee is a martial artist taught by her father. After Emperor Chang Wu had her father short, she became a freedom fighter opposing the false emperor's rule. In all versions of the story, Jing Lee helps the heroic adventurers find the Dragon Fortress and recover the Golden Dragon, although details differ between various media.

entities.name: Johnny Thunder
entities.description:
Johnny Thunder, also known by other names such as Sam Grant, Joe Freeman, and Sawyer, is the main protagonist of the LEGO Adventurers theme. He is included in numerous sets as a minifigure in each of the theme's sub-themes, often alongside his friends Dr. Kilroy and Pippin Reed. He also appears in a couple Studios sets as an actor. In addition to all of this, Johnny also appears in twelve video games released across multiple platforms, more than any other LEGO character.

He reappears in 2014 in The LEGO Movie, as well as one of the sets based on the same movie, 70815 Super Secret Police Dropship. Johnny Thunder also appears in 71025 Minifigures Series 19 as the Jungle Explorer, who was confirmed to be an updated version by graphics/minifigure designer Austin William Carlson. Another updated Johnny minifigure appears in the 2024 City Explorer subtheme, with his identity confirmed by model designer Rik Pauwels, LEGO Party!, and the 60470 Explorer Train product description.

In his appearances in the Desert, Jungle, and Dino Island subthemes and the Studios theme, Johnny wears black pants and a brick yellow button-up shirt. The shirt has two pockets on the chest, a black belt with a revolver in it, and a red bandana around his neck. Above the bandanna, a little bit of his yellow chest is showing. His sleeves are also brick yellow and his hands are bright yellow. Johnny's face has a black mustache, sideburns, hair, and a smirk. He wears an earth orange Safari Hat resembling an Australian slouch hat folded up on one side. Some of Johnny's variants also have an earth orange backpack attached to the neck between the head and torso.

In the Orient Expedition theme, Johnny was redesigned and received three new variants for each of the areas he and his partners visited. On all three variants, Johnny Thunder's face is updated and now has white pupils in his eyes, a more subtle smile rather than a smirk, and a cleft chin. He retains the earth orange slouch hat.

entities.name: Jun-Chi
entities.description:
Jun-Chi is an Adventurers Orient Expedition big figure introduced in 2003. He is exclusive to the set 7413 Passage of Jun-Chi.

Jun-Chi uses the same build as Tygurah and the Yeti and consists of six black pieces and one bright red piece. Legs and arms are attached to a body assembled from two Technic Brick 1X2, Ø4.9 and one Plate 2X2. This is covered by a single large bright red piece (unique to Jun-Chi) that comprises Jun-Chi's torso and head, which is molded in the likeness of a Shisa. His torso features blue and gold printing, and his head has white eyes, white teeth, and some blue hair.

The Jun-Chi is a large monster based on the Chinese myth of the Shisa, a half-lion, half-dog deity. He guards the Passage of Jun-Chi, which is portrayed in the online and magazine comics as a secret entrance to the Dragon Fortress; his appearance is so dreaded that even Dragon Fortress Guards avoid the passage. He gives chase to the Adventurers when they pass through. Shortly afterward, Jun-Chi barges into the Dragon Fortress, scattering the guards and allowing the Adventurers and Lord Sam Sinister to escape amidst the chaos.

In the 7413 set comic, Jun-Chi appears when Johnny Thunder tries to grab a ruby from the Passage of Jun-Chi, causing the revolving wall to spin around. Johnny escapes Jun-Chi by blocking the wall with a torch.
entities.short_description: Jun-Chi is an Adventurers Orient Expedition big figure introduced in 2003. He is exclusive to the set 7413 Passage of Jun-Chi.

entities.name: Lord Sam Sinister
entities.description:
Lord Sam Sinister, also known by many other names including Baron von Barron (or Baron von Baron), Sam Sinister (or Sam Sanister), Evil Eye, Mr. Hates, and Samuel von Barron, is the main villain from the Adventurers and Orient Expedition themes. Sinister competes with Johnny Thunder in all of the Adventurers sub-themes (except for the 1999 Jungle theme) as they search for ancient artifacts and treasures from around the world.

In Adventurers, Sam Sinister has a dark grey hook in place of his left hand. He has a monocle over his right eye, a large handlebar mustache (depicted as mutton chops in World Club Magazine Time Cruisers comics), and a scar on his left cheek. He generally wears a brick yellow khaki shirt, a black glove on his right hand, a pair of white epaulets, and either a white pith helmet or a grey or earth orange aviator helmet.

In LEGO Racers, his in-game model does not have epaulets, much like Captain Redbeard. In LEGO Racers 2, his epaulets and hook are missing from his model, leading him to be depicted with two normal hands. In the intro cutscene of LEGO Stunt Rally, his left hand is a regular black hand instead of a hook; his right hand is obscured, leaving it possible that his hand and hook were erroneously swapped.

In renders for LEGO Racers and Rocket Racers, Baron von Barron is portrayed with a mirrored face print that is missing his mouth, no epaulets, and a regular bright yellow hand instead of a black glove. This design also appears in at least one of the clips of the Rocket Racers queue video. However, other Rocket Racers clips depict von Barron's design matching his physical minifigure, albeit with a fully-modeled transparent monocle instead of a printed opaque one.

entities.name: Maharaja Lallu
entities.description:
Maharaja Lallu, simply referred to as the Maharaja in most media, is an Orient Expedition minifigure introduced in 2003.

Maharaja Lallu wears a white turban. His face is printed with grey hair poking out from under his turban; his hair stretches into a full, grey beard and moustache. He has two black eyes and a stern mouth. Lallu wears dark orange robes with ovular decorations. He has a red belt above his waist where a knife is tucked in.

In LEGO Rock Band, the Indian King lacks any facial hair and has black eyebrows, but is otherwise identical to Maharaja Lallu's physical minifigure.

Maharaja Lallu is a greedy and ruthless Indian tyrant who rules the Scorpion Palace and demands grain from the poor villagers. He joins forces with Lord Sam Sinister in search of Marco Polo's Golden Shield, a treasure that was hidden in the Scorpion Palace unbeknownst to Lallu.

entities.name: Mike
entities.description:
Mike (misnamed Harry Cane in 5784 Soccer Mania) is an Adventurers Dino Island minifigure introduced in 2000. He appears in several Adventurers sets, as well as having an appearance in the video game LEGO Racers 2.

Mike wears an earth orange vest over a white shirt, grey pants, and an earth orange Western Cap. His torso is also printed with two buttons on his shirt collar, a grey rope belt, and a slingshot tucked into his belt. His face is printed with black hair, eyebrows, freckles, and dimples that give him a youthful appearance.

As a Studios actor, Mike wears a bright red Safari Hat, and the back of his torso is printed with the LEGO logo.

In 5784 Soccer Mania, Harry Cane retains Mike's head but otherwise has a completely different outfit. He has a brick yellow jacket worn over a light green and dark green striped shirt, black pants, and an earth orange Safari Hat. Since "Harry Cane" has Mike's face while the real Harry Cane appears in the same game as "Billy Speed", this character is most likely intended to represent Mike.
entities.short_description: Mike (misnamed Harry Cane in 5784 Soccer Mania) is an Adventurers Dino Island minifigure introduced in 2000. He appears in several Adventurers sets, as well as having an appearance in the video game LEGO Racers 2.

entities.name: Minotaur
entities.description:
The Minotaur, also called The Guardian of the Golden Bull, was a character in one of the two online games Johnny Thunder and the Adventurers. The Minotaur first appeared in the online game as an enemy in the labyrinth and then played against Johnny Thunder in a modified game of Connect Four for the possession of a legendary artifact, the Golden Bull.

According to the game's cutscenes, the Minotaur's origins are the same as in Greek Mythology-Minos, king of the island of Crete cheated the god of the sea, Poseidon, in a bargain. To gain his revenge, Poseidon put a curse on Minos' wife which caused her to fall in love with a beautiful bull Minos was supposed to sacrifice to Poseidon. When Minos' wife gave birth to a beast-half man and half-bull. Minos' had a labyrinth built to hide the beast, which had been dubbed the Minotaur (Greek for bull of Minos).

However, the game adds a twist onto the myth. According to Dr. Kilroy, a sacred artifact, known as the golden bull was hidden in the maze, guarded by the Minotaur. The adventurers discovered that the golden bull was not actually in the maze, but a clue was. The adventurers traveled to a nearby island seen in a mural in the labyrinth. Johnny Thunder scaled the cliff to discover a temple. Hidden behind the veil was the shadow of a bull like creature (presumably the Minotaur) who claimed to be "The guardian on the Golden Bull". The guardian challenged Johnny to a modified game of Connect Four. Johnny won, and was awarded with the golden bull.

entities.name: Mr. Cunningham
entities.description:
Mr. Cunningham is a villainous minifigure from the Adventurers theme in 2000. He is included in three different LEGO sets.

Mr. Cunningham wears a dark grey jacket over a grey-and-red striped shirt that exposes his belly button, implying that he is overweight. He wears earth orange pants, with 5955 All Terrain Trapper having a black hip piece and other sets having an earth orange hip. His hat is an earth orange Safari Hat. His face is printed with brown sideburns, eyebrows, a mustache, and stubble.

Mr. Cunningham is a tough henchman working for Sam Sinister and Alexia Sinister in their plot to capture dinosaurs from Dino Island. According to LEGO Mania Magazine, he is a master of disguise and has been known to change his disguises weekly.

In The Championship Challenge, Mr. Cunningham gets into a fight with Dr. Lightning in the stands after Sam Sinister tackles an all-star player. In Double Trouble on Dino Island, Mr. Cunningham flies the Research Glider and informs Sinister about Johnny Thunder and Mike making a crash-landing on Dino Island.
entities.short_description: Mr. Cunningham is a villainous minifigure from the Adventurers theme in 2000. He is included in three different LEGO sets.

entities.name: Ngan Pa
entities.description:
Ngan Pa is an Adventurers Orient Expedition minifigure released in 2003. He is exclusive to the set 7417 Temple of Mount Everest.

Ngan Pa has dark grey legs and an earth orange torso. He wears a fur-lined jacket which has a black belt and striped top underneath, and has dark red arms with black gloves. His face is yellow, and he has a small black Fu Manchu-style mustache. He wears a large furry black hat.

Although consistently portrayed with dark grey legs in most LEGO media, an alternate printing of the 7417 Temple of Mount Everest building instructions' page 6 portrays him with grey legs instead, which are swapped with Sherpa Sangye Dorje. Both printings show him with the correct dark grey legs on page 45.

Ngan Pa is a very greedy Yeti hunter, working for Lord Sam Sinister in exchange for treasure during the search for the Temple of Mount Everest. This makes him an enemy of Johnny Thunder.
entities.short_description: Ngan Pa is an Adventurers Orient Expedition minifigure released in 2003. He is exclusive to the set 7417 Temple of Mount Everest.

entities.name: Palace Guard
entities.description:
The Palace Guard, or simply Guard, is an Adventurers Orient Expedition minifigure released in 2003.

The Palace Guard wears a black turban, dark grey pants, and a bright blue shirt with a green silk belt and red diamond-shaped decorations. He has a small dagger in his belt. His hair is black, and some of it peeks out of his turban. He has lots of black stubble and a smirking expression.

In Secret of Scorpion Palace, the Guards wear black robes with yellow belts and trimmings and a blue scorpion emblem on their backs.

The Palace Guards, as their title suggests, guard the Scorpion Palace. They act as the evil minions of Maharaja Lallu. In the online comics and 4215473 Die Suche nach dem Goldenen Drachen, two Guards hold Babloo prisoner while Lallu interrogates him, and they are ordered to chase after Johnny Thunder when he rescues the boy. In the 7418 set comic, a Guard helps Lallu and Lord Sam Sinister capture Johnny Thunder and Dr. Kilroy, but he is chased away by the rolling boulder; in Die Suche nach dem Goldenen Drachen, the Guards are unable to stop Babloo and his elephants from overthrowing the Maharaja.
entities.short_description: The Palace Guard, or simply Guard, is an Adventurers Orient Expedition minifigure released in 2003.

entities.description:

Pharaoh Hotep, also known as Pharaoh's Mummy, Pharaoh Ramses III, Pharaoh Ramses IV, and Eddie Elbow, is a minifigure in the Adventurers Desert theme, being first introduced in 1998.

Hotep has a dark green hip and black legs, printed with a green sash and grey toes. His torso is black, and printed with blue armor and a red-and-gold collar. His arms are black, and his hands bright red. His face is grey and printed with a smiling, stitched-up mouth, with skull-like nostrils and dark eyes outlined in red. On his forehead, above his eyebrows, is a scar which has been sewn shut. He wears a bright yellow nemes with blue and gold stripes printed on it. Notably, this minifigure's printed toes and nostrils are rare features among minifigures.

Pharaoh Hotep was buried in the Pharaoh's Forbidden Ruins, where his undead mummy guards the ancient Re-Gou Ruby and wards off anyone who tries to steal it.

entities.name: Pharaoh Skeleton
entities.description:
Pharaoh Skeleton is a minifigure introduced in 1998 that appears in many Adventurers Desert sets.

The Pharaoh Skeleton is a skeleton, with the same white body, ball-jointed arms, and printed skull face as all other skeletons since their debut in 1995. These skeletons uniquely wear nemes headdresses; the nemes may be bright yellow with gold and blue stripes, bright yellow, or white.

A Pharaoh Skeleton guards an ancient treasure chamber in the oasis. In Johnny Thunder and the Lost Ruby, the Adventurers discover a Pharaoh Skeleton with a map in its sarcophagus, and they take the skeleton to the museum while Johnny Thunder follows the map. He encounters another Pharaoh Skeleton at the sphinx, guarding another map inside its sarcophagus.

The Mummy's Curse power up in LEGO Racers features the Pharaoh Skeleton's skull and nemes. It is a hazard that can be dropped by collecting a yellow brick with three white bricks. There are green flames under the skull of Pharaoh Skeleton when deployed. When another racer touches the trap, the skull will start circling around the green-tinted car with a distorted sound while the Mummy's Curse reverses the car's steering so the racer cannot drive normally for a few seconds. If someone else bumps into the cursed driver, they are also afflicted by the Mummy's Curse.

entities.name: Pippin Reed
entities.description:
Pippin Reed (or Pippin Read), formerly known by various other names including Gail Storm and Linda Lovely, is a Adventurers minifigure introduced in 1998.

Pippin Reed's original Desert minifigure wears a white pith helmet; a brick yellow button-down shirt with pockets, a red scarf, and a blue camera strapped around her collar; and bright red pants. Her face is printed with brown hair, black eyelashes, and red lips. In the Jungle subtheme, her torso was changed to a dark green jacket worn over a white button-down shirt with a necklace and silver camera. Her appearance in remained largely unchanged, although she sometimes wears an earth orange aviator's helmet with black goggles; she also wears this helmet in LEGO Island 2 and Soccer Mania.

In The Curse of the Mummy - An Interactive Puzzle Book, Pippin Read's appearance is based on her Desert minifigure with two notable differences. Her pants are brick yellow instead of bright red, and instead of a pith helmet, she has a molded hairpiece that appears to be based on the hair on her face printing. These unique elements are dropped by the sequel, The Lost Temple - An Interactive Puzzle Book, which faithfully represents her Jungle minifigure.

In Studios, Pippin Reed's design is derived from her Desert minifigure with some alterations. In 1354 Dino Head Attack, she wears an earth orange slouch hat and black pants. In Jurassic Park III, she wears a white U.S. Cap and an earth orange backpack.
entities.short_description: Pippin Reed (or Pippin Read), formerly known by various other names including Gail Storm and Linda Lovely, is a Adventurers minifigure introduced in 1998.

entities.name: Rudo Villano
entities.description:
Rudo Villano, also known as Max Villano in the United Kingdom, is a villain from the Adventurers Jungle theme introduced in 1999.

Rudo Villano wears a black Safari Hat and has messy, black hair sticking out from under it. His eyes are slanted in an angry expression and a red scar is slashed under his right one. His face is given stubble detailing. Villano wears a dark grey button-up shirt which exposes skin near the top, also revealing chest hair. A cartridge belt is printed above his waist and two revolvers are pushed in it. He has earth orange pants and, in some appearances, also has a matching backpack.

In Tales on the LEGO Express: The Heist, Rudo Villano wears a black neck scarf, covering the lower half of his face.

His appearance in 5784 Soccer Mania is slightly changed. Rather than wearing a fedora, he has a dark grey cap similar to Docs. His torso is also modified; his shirt is now fully unbuttoned, showing a green-and-black striped undershirt, and his two revolvers are absent.
entities.short_description: Rudo Villano, also known as Max Villano in the United Kingdom, is a villain from the Adventurers Jungle theme introduced in 1999.

entities.name: Sherpa Sangye Dorje
entities.description:
Sherpa Sangye Dorje is an Orient Expedition minifigure introduced in 2003. He is exclusive to the set 7417 Temple of Mount Everest.

The Sherpa has unprinted grey legs, and a dark orange torso decorated with a baggy shirt, a red sash, and a dagger. His arms are dark orange, and his hands are bright yellow. His face is bright yellow as well, and he has large eyes. He wears a large orange orange hat and an earth orange backpack.

Although consistently portrayed with grey legs in most LEGO media, an alternate printing of the 7417 Temple of Mount Everest building instructions' page 6 portrays him with dark grey legs instead, which are swapped with Ngan Pa. Both printings show him with the correct grey legs on page 45.

Sangye Dorje is a young Tibetan Sherpa who assists Johnny Thunder and his friends on Mount Everest during their quest for the Golden Sword.
entities.short_description: Sherpa Sangye Dorje is an Orient Expedition minifigure introduced in 2003. He is exclusive to the set 7417 Temple of Mount Everest.

entities.name: Skeleton
entities.description:
A Skeleton is a minifigure that appears in various themes in many sets. It was the first in a long line of skeletons (see the Skeleton Disambiguation page) and feature ball and socket joints and rounded eyes. Since their debut in Pirates and Castle in 1995, skeletons have appeared in a wide variety of themes to this day. Skeletons are also playable characters in video games for comical purposes, only playable under the "Extra Toggle" feature.

The body form of the skeleton has slightly changed over the years. For instance, the first LEGO skeletons had arms with ball and socket joints which allowed them to move all the way out to the side and all the way around. Skeletons in later sets had arms with normal pivot joints, like on a Battle Droid, that just move up and down. Also, the faces changed in the Castle sets. Classic skeletons had round eyes which gave them a neutral or even friendlier look to their faces than in the newer skeleton that has a slanted or evil look in their eyes. A new variation of the skeleton was released in the Ninjago theme, which feature redesigned torsos, arms and legs.

entities.name: Slyboots
entities.description:
Slyboots (or Sly Boots), also known by many other names including Sam Sinister and Lizard Boots, is a villain in Adventurers Desert theme. He initially appeared alongside Baron von Barron, although he was dropped out of set releases in later subthemes while Baron von Barron became the main villain of the Adventurers series. However, Slyboots still appeared regularly in video games and other Adventurers media.

Slyboots is dressed entirely in black, wearing a Top Hat - Mini Figure and a suit jacket over a collared red shirt. His face is printed with thick eyebrows, handlebar mustache, and goatee, and he wears a pair of glasses with large round white lens over his eyes.

When portrayed as a human in the Time Cruisers comic, Sly Boots has a large, physically-imposing build in order to reflect his backstory as a former prizefighter.

In the intro cutscene of LEGO Stunt Rally, Slyboots is wearing Baron von Barron's outfit: a white pith helmet, a brick yellow safari shirt, and grey pants. Unlike von Barron, Slyboots does not wear epaulets and both his hands are regular bright yellow hands instead of a hook or black glove.

entities.name: Tygurah
entities.description:
Tygurah is an Adventurers Orient Expedition Big Figure introduced in 2003. It is exclusive to the set 7411 Tygurah's Roar.

Tygurah uses the same build as the Yeti and Jun-Chi and consists of eight light orange brown pieces. Legs and arms are attached to a body assembled from two Technic Brick 1X2, Ø4.9 and one Plate 2X2. This is covered by a single large piece (unique to Tygurah) that comprises his torso and the tiger-shaped head; this piece is printed with white fur, black tiger stripes, and a black nose on the head. A light orange brown tail is attached to his back, which gives Tygurah one more piece than either the Yeti or Jun-Chi.

The Tygurah is a large Indian creature that resembles a humanoid tiger. He guards the Sunstone at an altar that has a bridge spanning a large chasm. According to Babloo in 4215473 Die Suche nach dem Goldenen Drachen, Tygurah acts in service to the gods by protecting the Sunstone, which brings good weather and harvest, and one knows that Tygurah is near when his roar can be heard.

After Maharaja Lallu demands that Babloo bring him the Sunstone, the Adventurers volunteer to help Babloo. Dr. Kilroy discovers the altar and encounters Tygurah, who gives chase. In the comics, the bridge breaks when Tygurah stands on it and he falls through, prompting Kilroy to remark that the "Tygurah needs a diet"; Episode 02 shows Tygurah disappearing into the chasm below, while the 7411 comic merely shows Tygurah becoming dazed. The audio drama does not show Tygurah's defeat at all, and Kilroy hears his roar throughout the night.
entities.short_description: Tygurah is an Adventurers Orient Expedition Big Figure introduced in 2003. It is exclusive to the set 7411 Tygurah's Roar.

entities.name: Tyrannosaurus rex
entities.description:
The Tyrannosaurus rex, or T. rex (written colloquially as T-Rex in most LEGO media prior to Jurassic World), is a LEGO Animal dinosaur, usually made of multiple parts. Since the first T. rex was released in 1997 in DUPLO, various incarnations and versions of the T. rex have been released since.

The first T-Rex figures appeared in 1997 in the preschool targeted DUPLO theme. The figure was part of DUPLOs new Dino theme, and was only one single piece with no movable parts. The original DUPLO Tyrannosaurs only came in red, and in two sizes: an adult T-Rex, and a baby T-Rex.

In 1999, blue colored baby DUPLO T-Rex were made available in the sets 2803 Dinosaur Babies and 2821 Dinosaurs Fun Forest.

A green colored DUPLO T-Rex was produced in 2002 for the set 3615 Theatre Stories.

entities.name: Yeti
entities.description:
The Yeti is an Adventurers Big Figure introduced in 2003 based on a Himalayan myth. The Yeti is exclusive to the set 7412 Yeti's Hideout.

The Yeti uses the same build as Tygurah and Jun-Chi and consists of seven white pieces. Legs and arms are attached to a body assembled from two Technic Brick 1X2, Ø4.9 and one Plate 2X2. This is covered by a single large piece (unique to the Yeti) that comprises the Yeti's furry torso and the head, which is molded in a gape-mouthed expression. In some official photos (such as the set's alternate models), the Yeti wields at least one club as a weapon.

The Yeti is a mythical ape-like creature from the Himalaya mountain range, and is both feared and respected by local villagers, to whom it is known as "Rakshasa". Although it is considered a sacred creature to the Sherpa, Ngan Pa seeks to hunt the Yeti.

While on Mount Everest, Pippin Reed is attracted to a shrine where she finds an emerald. The angry Yeti emerges from its cave and gives chase to Pippin. She managed to escape with the emerald by stunning the Yeti with the flash on her camera. In 4215473 Die Suche nach dem Goldenen Drachen, the blinded Yeti hits its head on a rock and knocks itself out, and at Sherpa Sangye Dorje's insistence, the adventurers bandage its head before leaving. In Episode Three: Mystery on Mount Everest, the heroes are chased by the Yeti again, forcing them to hurry to the Temple of Mount Everest.
entities.short_description: The Yeti is an Adventurers Big Figure introduced in 2003 based on a Himalayan myth. The Yeti is exclusive to the set 7412 Yeti's Hideout.

entities.description:
8635 Mission 6: Mobile Command Base 8636 Mission 7: Deep Sea Quest 8971 Aerial Defense Unit

Agent Charge is an Agents minifigure introduced in 2008. He has been in four sets during 2008 and one in Agents 2.0 during 2009.

In 8971 Aerial Defense Unit, he wore body armour.

Agent Charge can pilot sea, air, and land vehicles, and he is an engineering-systems specialist.

entities.name: Agent Chase
entities.description:
Agent Chase is the main protagonist in the themes Agents and Agents 2.0.

Chase has a dual-sided face: on the front side, he is seen with tinted sunglasses and a smirking expression; on the flip side of his head, he is seen without glasses and with a frowning mouth. In the sets 8633 Mission 4: Speedboat Rescue and 8636 Mission 7: Deep Sea Quest, as well as LEGO Battles: Ninjago, he has only his alternate frowning face, which is a common head used in other LEGO themes.

Agent Chase is a team leader and top field agent who specializes in hazardous missions. He is experienced with life-threatening situations while always remaining calm, although he will act with urgency when necessary. He quickly comes up with plans and finds solutions to his problems.

Agent Chase partakes in six of the original eight missions. In Mission 1, Agent Chase chases Saw Fist in a Jetpack. In Mission 4, Chase has to rescue Agent Trace from Break Jaw and his robotic sharks. In Mission 5, Chase must steal a laptop containing Dr. Inferno's latest plans for taking over the world. In Mission 6, Chase and his fellow Agents have to stop Dr. Inferno from escaping the High-Security Jail built into the center. In Mission 7, Chase has to recover some treasure. In Mission 8, Chase has to rescue Agent Fuse as well as destroying the laser of Dr. Inferno's Volcano Base hideout.
entities.short_description: Agent Chase is the main protagonist in the themes Agents and Agents 2.0.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. LEGO art © The LEGO Group (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Agent Fuse
entities.description:
Agent Fuse is an Agents minifigure introduced in 2008.

In Agents 2.0, he wears body armour. Like other Agents, he has a dual-sided head, with the reverse side of his face showing him scared.

Agent Fuse is the team's computer, electronics, and explosives specialist. He is also a talented pilot.

In 2854298 The Adventures of Clutch Powers, he appears three different times. He first appears in the chapter "The LEGO Team," while walking down the street. Fuse appears again in the same chapter, watching the Grand Carousel. Fuse again appears in the chapter "Space Mission," waving Clutch and his team goodbye as they ride in the Galactic Enforcer.
entities.short_description: Agent Fuse is an Agents minifigure introduced in 2008.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. LEGO art © The LEGO Group (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Agent Swift
entities.description: Lego Agents (stylized as LEGO Agents) is a discontinued Lego theme that was first introduced in June 2008 after the discontinued Lego Alpha Team theme. The theme was inspired by James Bond as well as various spy movies. The 13 toy sets in the theme's release were split into three waves. In 2009, the theme was re-branded as Lego Agents 2.0. It was discontinued by the end of 2009 and replaced with the Lego Ultra Agents theme in 2014.

The minifigure was produced with blond hair, the same mould that was used for Agent Charge's hair piece, the Agent torso and legs design and the minifigure is equipped with a "bullet-proof vest". The face design is unique to this character it shows cheek bones, brown eyebrows, and a communication device.

entities.description:
Agent Trace is a character in the Agents series. She is featured in four sets, including one in Agents 2.0.

She is specialized in security, code decryption, and secret undercover missions. Although she is a capable agent, she serves the role of the damsel in distress in Mission 4.

Security, decryption and undercover-mission specialist.

entities.name: Break Jaw
entities.description:
His name is "Break Jaw" because he wears a metal helmet with an underbite. He has the standard suit of an Inferno Henchman. He also has the same helmet as the Magma Commander. He has been featured in several plots by Dr. Inferno. His first "starter" mission was to locate and study a treasure map deep in a swamp. But that plot was foiled by Agent Charge who burst into Break Jaw's camp with his motorcycle. Break Jaw escaped in his mini-boat but the map was retrieved by Charge. Dr. Inferno was happy with his performance and sent him with a prisoner (Agent Trace) to a buoy sort of base and started to feed her to sharks. But Agent Chase came in a boat and saved Trace. Dr. Inferno was not happy, but he gave Break Jaw one more chance. He sent him to work alongside Slime Face in a mission to recover a gem chest deep in the ocean. Break Jaw came and him and Slime Face fought well, but the chest was taken by Charge and Chase. Break Jaw, along with Slime Face, was retired from Dr. Inferno's forces for their poor performance.

Category:Agents minifigures Category:Minifigures introduced in 2008

entities.name: Dollar Bill
entities.description:
Dollar Bill is a henchman of the evil Dr. Inferno. He appears in only one set, 8968 River Heist. He carries a golden gun and works alongside Dyna-Mite.

Dollar Bill has a green hairpiece, a yellow headpiece depicting a greedy expression (which is the same face as the Inferno Henchman apart from the diamond and no gold tooth), a mustache, and his left eye is composed of a diamond. He wears a black suit with an Inferno badge on the left side and a pocket filled with dollar bills on the right side, and has white hand pieces, showing he is wearing white gloves.

It is clear from his general demeanor that he is obsessed with money. Dr. Inferno thought he would be perfect to steal some money from a local bank, so he sent him along with Dyna-Mite to do the job. He was captured by Agent Fuse.

entities.name: Dr. D. Zaster
entities.description:
Dr. D. Zaster is an Agents 2.0 minifigure introduced in 2009.

Dr. D. Zaster is dressed in a black labcoat, which is a black version of Dr. Inferno's labcoat with green slime oozing down his torso. He has a transparent fluorescent green slime-coated face with a wide grin, a green right eye, and a red left eye; this is reused from Slime Face. His hair is a white Evil Wig 'no.2' with bright yellowish green highlights.

Dr. D. Zaster is an old friend of Dr. Inferno. D. Zaster plans to cover LEGO City with his Slime Chopper's toxic slime, but his plot is foiled by Agent Chase.

In The Robot Chronicles, Dr. D. Zaster pilots the Ace Slime Choppers, which must be defeated by the Agents in the mission "Battle for the Skies".

entities.name: Dr. Inferno
entities.description:
Dr. Inferno is an Agents minifigure introduced in 2008.

Dr. Inferno wears a white labcoat with printed orange lapels and belts as well as his insignia on his chest and on his back. He wears a black glove on his left hand. His right arm is a cool silver, drum lacquered robotic arm with a silver (in 2008) or cool silver, drum lacquered (in 2009) Stick Ø 3.2 W. Holder claw. His hair is Evil Wig 'No.1', which is black with bright orange highlights. His face is printed with arched eyebrows, a wide manic grin, and a scar over his white left eye.

Dr. Inferno is the main antagonist of the Agents theme and has been one of the LEGO Agents' most wanted villains since their formation. He is an evil genius who tries to take over the world with his crazy schemes to sow chaos with his technology, weaponry, and henchmen. His evil lair is the Volcano Base. He is old friends with Dr. D. Zaster.

In Mission 6, after Dr. Inferno's laptop was stolen by Agents, Dr. Inferno is cornered and captured by the Agents and held prisoner on their Mobile Command Center, but he breaks free with the help of his henchmen Gold Tooth and Spy Clops. In Mission 8, Dr. Inferno prepares to fire the laser atop his Volcano Base, but the Agents arrive to thwart his plans.
entities.short_description: Dr. Inferno is an Agents minifigure introduced in 2008.

2856195 LEGO Minifigure Ultimate Sticker Collection 852948 Female Magnet Set

Dyna-Mite is an Agents minifigure. She is especially known for her obsession with dynamite, thus the name Dyna-Mite. She has the same hair-piece as Irina Spalko, News Reporter, and Nya, except the colour is red.

entities.name: Fire Arm
entities.description:
Fire Arm is an Agents minifigure introduced in 2008.

Fire Arm has an orange and dark stone grey suit like most of Dr. Inferno's henchmen, with additional printing showing black portions of his uniform and silver robotics underneath. His hair is a black Mini Wig, Crewcut, a common hairpiece in the Agents theme. He is similar to Saw Fist, but has a cannon instead of a buzz saw on his mechanical right arm, and his face has cybernetics on the opposite side.

Fire Arm is one of Dr. Inferno's newest henchmen. Fire Arm and Claw-Dette captured Agent Fuse when he was on a solo mission. During the Agents' mission to infiltrate the Volcano Base, Fire Arm and Claw-Dette stood in their way of facing Dr. Inferno himself.

entities.name: Gold Tooth
entities.description:
Gold Tooth is a villain minifigure that appeared in the Agents and Agents 2.0 lines.

Gold Tooth wears a bright orange uniform with dark stone grey gloves and hip. His right leg and the right side of his torso are printed with zippers connecting to black portions of his uniform, and Dr. Inferno's emblem is on the left side of his torso and on his back. Gold Tooth's hair is an exclusive warm gold, drum lacquered Mini Wig, Crewcut. His face is printed with an eyepatch over his left eye and a wide grin showing off his all-gold teeth, albeit with one missing tooth on his upper jaw.

In 8635 Mission 6: Mobile Command Center, Gold Tooth wears a black Mini Crash Helmet with a warm gold Mini Visor 2.

Gold Tooth is Dr. Inferno's sneaky henchman who is obsessed with gold. In Mission 3, Gold Tooth and his Inferno Henchman steal gold bars from an ancient jungle temple and escape in their high-speed attack jeep, but they are hunted down by Agent Fuse's Supersonic Jet. In Mission 6, Gold Tooth and Spy Clops learn that Dr. Inferno is held prisoner aboard the Mobile Command Center, and they break him free.

entities.name: Inferno Henchman
entities.description:
The Inferno Henchman, or simply Henchman, is an Agents minifigure introduced in 2008.

The Inferno Henchman wears a black tuque and a bright orange zipsuit featuring the Inferno emblem on his torso. His hip and gloves are dark stone grey. He carries the same guns as the Agents and Dr. Inferno's other henchmen. He uses a common Crook face with stubble and a wide grin showing a gold tooth. Unlike most other Agents villains, this Henchman appears entirely human and is not a cyborg or mutant.

Inferno Henchmen are the foot soldiers of Dr. Inferno's army, assisting Gold Tooth and Spy Clops in their evil schemes.

The Magma Commander is a villain from the Agents theme. He is a cybernetic henchman of Dr. Inferno. He operates a hidden base close to the city from which he commands a horde of radio-controlled Magma Drones to attack it. The minifigure was first introduced in 2009, and has only been released in one set.

entities.description:
The Magma Drones are robots controlled and built by the Magma Commander.

They feature the special Agents robot arm on the end of which is a laser (an amber-coloured cone). Their "heads" consist of a black antenna/lever piece. They are controlled via the large satellite dish mounted on top of Magma Commander's base. The mission of the Agents in the Aerial Defence Unit was to destroy the satellite and shut the Magma Drones down. They were once used to siege LEGO City, but it is unknown if this plan succeeded.

entities.name: Saw Fist
entities.description:
Saw Fist is an Agents character. He is exclusive to Mission 1.

Saw Fist was one of Doctor Inferno's henchmen. Like most other henchmen of Dr. Inferno, Saw Fist is a cyborg. The left side of his face is metal, as is the right side of his body. Saw Fist has a robotic right arm with a chainsaw in place of a hand. His torso piece is also used for Fire-Arm. Dr. Inferno once ordered him to steal an energy crystal from a snowy mountain base. He fought his way through the defenses of the crystal vault and broke open the hatch, then grabbed the crystal and fleed down the snowy slopes in his snowmobile. He was foiled by Agent Chase in his heli-pack, who used a grappling hook to grab the crystal and fly away.

entities.name: Slime Face
entities.description:
Slime Face is an Agents minifigure introduced in 2008.

Slime Face is clad in a black diver's suit dripping with green slime, wears a transparent Insect Helm, and is equipped with a dark stone grey Oxygenbottle With Tube and black Swim Fins. He has a transparent fluorescent green slime-coated face with a wide grin, a green right eye, and a red left eye.

Slime Face is a genetically-altered henchman of the evil Dr. Inferno. In Mission 7, Slime Face and Break Jaw attempt to recover a sunken treasure chest full of diamonds in the ocean.

Slime Face Slime Face is one of Dr. Inferno's henchmen who has been genetically altered. His face is always covered with slime.

entities.name: Spy Clops
entities.description:
8635 Mission 6: Mobile Command Center Agents HQ

Spy Clops is one of Dr. Inferno's henchman. He has four eyes and six legs made from made from 'robot arm' pieces with horns on the tips, much like the legs of a spider. In the 8635 Mission 6: Mobile Command Center he comes with black legs, but in 8634 Mission 5: Turbocar Chase he comes with unique silver legs. He looks something like a claw. Dr. Inferno created him to work for him. The first plot Inferno used him for was to stop Agent Chase in his Turbocar. Spy Clops succeeded and got the laptop information from Chase. Then Dr. Inferno enlisted his help to get him out of captivity from the Agents Mobile Command Center.

Cyborg spy with mechanical spider-legs and all-seeing robotic eyes.

entities.description:
The ADU Pilot is an Alien Conquest minifigure introduced in 2011.

I’m just the guy for the job. No matter what or where, I’m always ready to hop into the nearest thing with wings and take the fight straight to the bad guys. G-forces? Disintegration beams? UFOs that can move faster than anything on the planet? They’re no match for this high-speed flyboy. Just point me at them and watch me clean up the sky!”

entities.description:
The ADU Rookie is an Alien Conquest minifigure introduced in 2011.

Ever since the aliens invaded my pop’s farm and stole his favorite cow, I’ve been itching to give them a little payback. And now that I’ve joined the A.D.U., I’m sure I’ll be saving the world in no time! The Sarge says I’ve got lots of potential, which is good, because I sort of keep getting in over my head and having to get rescued by the rest of the team. But I’m sure everybody starts out that way, right? I’m sure with a little practice, I’ll be beating the aliens in no time!”

The ADU Scientist is an Alien Conquest minifigure released in 2011. He has a white body with scientific features printed on his both sides of his torso, hips and legs. He uses a recolored version of Dastan's hair piece and sports new facial printing. The ADU Scientist has only appeared in one set.

entities.name: ADU Sergeant
entities.description:
The ADU Sergeant is an Alien Conquest minifigure introduced in 2011. He has a gruff expression with a grey mustache and thick eyebrows.

We are not here to be happy friendly people! We are not here to pet little puppies and kittens! We are here for one reason and one reason only: to fight those alien menaces and drive their entire fleet back into deep space! Help me do that and I will be your best friend! Mess up and I will be your worst nightmare! Now strap on your gear, start up your vehicles, and let’s go save the planet!”

entities.name: ADU Soldier
entities.description:
The ADU Soldier, named Deborah, is an Alien Conquest minifigure introduced in 2011.

The ADU Soldier wears a dark azur A.D.U. uniform with printing on the torso, hip, and legs; the torso print is shared with the ADU Rookie. Her gloves and hip are dark stone grey, while her helmet's visor is transparent. Her face has feminine lips and eyelashes, and features two facial expressions: one showing a confident smirk, the other showing a serious scowl.

Deborah is the Soldier of the Alien Defense Unit. She is proficient with A.D.U. weaponry and technology, and she is an enthusiastic fighter determined to prove that she is capable of completing her mission to stop as many alien invaders as she can. She eagerly requests the order to pilot the Interceptor Shuttle into battle against the Alien Mothership.

In LEGO Legacy: Heroes Unboxed, Deborah has been taken over by an Alien Clinger named Gorwell. Together, Deborah and Gorwell form an Explorer support unit with the abilities "Model 7066-1 Blaster", "Hive Mind's Orders", "Cerebral Feast", "Where Did All My Friends Go?", and "Mother Ship Backup".
entities.short_description: The ADU Soldier, named Deborah, is an Alien Conquest minifigure introduced in 2011.

entities.name: Alien Android
entities.description:
The Alien Android, also known as Alien Pirate and Alien Cyborg, is an Alien Conquest minifigure released in 2011. He appears exclusively to the set 7066 Earth Defense HQ.

The Alien Android has the same type of head as the Alien Commander and Alien Villainess, but with different printing. He also has multiple robotic body parts: a "metal" peg-leg, arm, and a cybernetic right eye, while the torso printing continues the half-cybernetic pattern. The head is made up of three elements; the face, a normal, transparent green minifigure head and the green brain piece, which fits over the skin and head.

Due to his computer brain, the Alien Android's space strategies exceed those of the Gixxl Prime robo-fleets,

"There are approximately 6.9 billion human beings on the planet Earth. By my calculations, the collected brainpower of the human population will be enough to power our invasion fleet for 82.4 galactic time units. Your planetary defenses stand zero chance of opposing the alien fleet. Do not attempt to stop us. Do not attempt to behave illogically. I assure you that unpredictable actions will not cre-ate feed-back in bzzt my cir-cuits kzzz blb Al-i-en An-droid sys-tem shut-ting down for re-boot zkt."
entities.short_description: The Alien Android, also known as Alien Pirate and Alien Cyborg, is an Alien Conquest minifigure released in 2011. He appears exclusively to the set 7066 Earth Defense HQ.

entities.name: Alien Clinger
entities.description:
7065 Alien Mothership 7066 Earth Defense HQ

The Alien Clinger, also known as Pluuvian Brain-Beast, is an Alien Conquest creature introduced in 2011. It is something of a mascot for the theme, and appear in three sets in total. LEGO Legacy: Heroes Unboxed features one specific Alien Clinger named Gorwell.

The Alien Clinger is a small, hollow, lime green creature with a hole in its bottom slightly larger than a minifigure's head, so it can be placed onto one. Its mouth is represented by another hole, this time on the front of the body, through which minifigures can see through. It has one eyestalk, on which it has a single printed eye. The six tentacles on its lower half can be used to hold it steady when placed on a flat surface, giving it a skittering appearance.

Pluuvian Brain-Beasts, colloquially known to humans as "Alien Clingers", are used by the alien invaders of Earth as special forces to control Earthlings' minds.

entities.name: Alien Commander
entities.description:
The Alien Commander, named Commander Hypaxxus-8 or Commander Z, is an Alien Conquest minifigure introduced in 2011.

The Alien Commander has a red cape and his brain is visible. He has the same shape of head as the Alien Cyborg, and the same shape of legs as the Squid Warrior, except that they are reversed. The left eye has a long streak across it; probably resembling a scar or a mark. He also has golden epaulettes, as seen on soldiers from the Pirates theme, and his head is made up of three parts.

In LEGO Minifigures Online, Commander Z has regular black legs.

The Alien Commander is the main antagonist who leads the alien conquest of Earth. He pilots the Alien Mothership and has a pet Alien Clinger that is named Captain Ploovie.

entities.name: Alien Pilot
entities.description:
The Alien Pilot is an Alien Conquest minifigure released in 2011. These troops specialize in piloting Alien spacecraft, and work in the air and in space, while their counterparts, the Alien Troopers, work on land. They talk in a fast, high-pitched voice.

The Alien Pilot has black legs, printed with a silver device, silver wires, and a small medium lilac area. He has a black torso, printed with silver tubes and a silver device, which is possibly a life-support unit. He has purple arms, and Lime Green hands. A uniquely moulded head is placed upon the torso, and features a visible brain at the back of the mould, and large black eyes.

The Alien Pilots are the aerial unit of the Alien army, and pilot most of the army's vehicles.

“Dude! I love being an Alien Pilot! We get to fly fast, fast, fast all the time! We’ve got super-quick turbo-charged hyper-reflexes, so nothing moves faster than us! Hey, wanna race? You’ll never win, because we can out-run, out-fly and out-zap anything in the sky! Some of the other aliens complain that us Pilots never stop talking, but that’s their own problem, right? We should totally have a race, dude! Bet I can collect more brainpower than you! Wooooooo!”

entities.name: Alien Trooper
entities.description:
Alien Trooper is an Alien Conquest minifigure that was introduced in 2011.

The Alien Troopers have black legs, printed with medium lilac padding. Their torsos are also black, and are printed with a large silver device (possibly a life-support unit), and more padding. They have purple arms, and Lime Green hands. Their Lime Green heads are uniquely molded, and show a large toothy mouth, big black eyes, and the upper area of an exposed brain.

The Alien Troopers are the bulk of the alien army, and primarily fight on land, although they are sometimes seen piloting vehicles.

"Hey, you! Yeah, you! You look like you got a pretty big brain, huh? Lots of thinking going on in there. Us Alien Troopers, we don’t gotta do a lot of thinking. But we’re really good at taking orders and shouting and smashing stuff. Oh, and shooting our lasers! Pyew, pyew! Like that! Sometimes it’s hard to remember which end of the laser to point away from us. That’s why our brains are no good for powering flying saucers. So we came to Earth to get yours! Now hand over all of your brains, or, uh…or else!”

entities.name: Farmer
entities.description:
The Farmer is an Alien Conquest minifigure released in May 2011. He is exclusive to the set 7052 UFO Abduction.

The Farmer wears worn-out blue overalls over a white-and-blue checkered shirt. His pants have patches, and several pieces of wheat are caught in his clothes. He has a single-sided headpiece with a beard and a terrified expression, and holds a brown pitchfork.

entities.name: Lotta Brix
entities.description:
Lotta Brix, commonly referred to as the Reporter, is a female minifigure from the Alien Conquest theme, exclusive to the set 7065 Alien Mothership.

Lotta Brix comes with a clipboard tile and the same microphone used by the Pop Star from 8684 Minifigures Series 2, and the Rapper from 8803 Minifigures Series 3. She has a double-sided headpiece. Her torso is printed with a red jacket and an identity badge. She uses the same hair piece as Agent Swift, Claw-Dette and Dyna-Mite from Agents.

Lotta Brix has written newspaper articles for Chicago Mercury-Pluto-Moon-Gazette and The Washington Click. One chronicled her experience with the Alien Mothership in Chicago, and the other featured her interviewing the Alien Commander at the Washington D.C. Capital Building.

entities.name: Arrow
entities.description:
Arrow is an Alpha Team Mission Deep Freeze minifigure that was introduced in 2004.

Arrow wears a black Mini Pixie Cap and the black standard Mission Deep Freeze Alpha Team uniform with a bright yellow right sleeve. His face is printed with long black hair, a very wide mouth, and a scowling facial expression, and he is equipped with a silver microphone and a device over his right eye.

Arrow is Alpha Team's mechanic, filling the role of Cam Attaway from previous missions.

In the 4746 Mobile Command Center comic, Arrow and Charge set out in snow scooters to investigate an Ice Drone planting an Ice Orb in the snow. In the 4748 Ogel's Mountain Fortress comic, Arrow is frozen in an ice block outside Ogel's fortress, but he is rescued by Dash Justice.
entities.short_description: Arrow is an Alpha Team Mission Deep Freeze minifigure that was introduced in 2004.

entities.name: Cam Attaway
entities.description:
Cam Attaway, often simply called Cam, is an Alpha Team minifigure introduced in 2000 before making her physical debut in 2001.

In 5714 LEGO Alpha Team, Cam wears a black Alpha Team uniform with red as her secondary color on her right side. She wears a sleeveless shirt, exposing her bright yellow arms. Her torso is decorated with a chain necklace, the Alpha Team emblem, and a dark grey work vest equipped with an oil can and three wrenches. Her legs have pouches and kneepads. She has short bright red hair with black tips. Her face has red lipstick, blue sunglasses, feminine eyelashes, angled eyebrows, and a microphone headset.

Cam's first physical minifigure recreates her design from the video game, but greatly simplifies the details on her work vest and changes the shape of the oil canister. Her hair is a bright red Mini Wig, Girl and loses the black tips. Her blue sunglasses are clear with purple tints, and she has purple eyeshadow.

In Mission Deep Sea, Cam has wears an earth blue wetsuit without any of the mechanic gear from her previous iterations. Her torso has a zipper that is partially unzipped, barely revealing a white undershirt. The Alpha Team logo has been moved to her left breast, and a pair of zipper pockets have been added directly beneath. She has a utility belt and leg printing similar to other Alpha Team agents. Her hair color has been changed to dark red, her sunglasses have been removed, and she now has green eyes with red eyeshadow. Her hair can alternatively be replaced with a dark grey scuba airtank and helmet with a transparent blue visor.
entities.short_description: Cam Attaway, often simply called Cam, is an Alpha Team minifigure introduced in 2000 before making her physical debut in 2001.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. LEGO art © The LEGO Group (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Charge
entities.description:
Charge, also known as Lexon in Germany, is an Alpha Team minifigure first introduced in a 2000 video game before making a physical debut in 2001.

In the 5714 LEGO Alpha Team PC game, Charge wears a black jumpsuit, with the right side of his torso being colored blue. He has the Alpha Team logo on the left side of his torso, a power cable slung over his right shoulder, and a battery and charge meter strapped to his belt. His right sleeve is bright blue. His legs feature textured pads on his hips, thighs, and shins, along with a blue stripe along his right side. He has black hair shaped as a crew cut. His face is textured with sunglasses, sideburns, a mustache, a goatee, stubble, and a headset with a microphone.

When Charge made his physical debut in 2001, his minifigure design was based upon his video game model with some changes. His torso print was slightly modified, removing the power cable and changing the yellow/black stripes on the battery to blue/grey. His thigh pads have been changed to pockets. His hair is represented by a Mini Wig Man, despite the same theme also featuring the newly-introduced Mini Wig, Crewcut.

Charge's Mission Deep Sea variant retains much of his 2001 minifigure design, with the most notable changes being switching black to earth blue and different leg printing that matches other Alpha Team agents in the subtheme. He wears dark grey Mini Crash Helmet with a transparent blue Divers Mask, with his black Mini Wig Man supplied as an alternative hair piece. A promotional image depicts him with a dark grey oxygen tank, but this is not included in Charge's only set within this subtheme.
entities.short_description: Charge, also known as Lexon in Germany, is an Alpha Team minifigure first introduced in a 2000 video game before making a physical debut in 2001.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. LEGO art © The LEGO Group (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Crunch
entities.description:
Crunch, also known as Tanxx in Germany and Сапер (Saper, "Sapper") in Russian, is an Alpha Team minifigure first introduced in a 2000 video game before making a physical debut in 2001.

In the 5714 LEGO Alpha Team PC game, Crunch wears a black jumpsuit with what appears to be a green overalls or vest worn over it. He has the Alpha Team insignia on the center of his chest, two sticks of dynamite on his vest, and a tool with a circular gauge. His right sleeve is dark green and his gloves are grey. His legs feature multiple tears. He wears a black Mini Headsquare Scarf; although its in-game model is simplified, it is more recognizable as the physical piece in the box art. His face is textured with a lowered brow, a wide mouth, a chin line, stubble, and a headset with a microphone.

When Crunch made his physical debut in 2001, his minifigure design was based upon his video game model with some minor color differences, such as his left shoulder strap being dark green instead of grey.

Crunch's Mission Deep Sea variant retains much of his 2001 minifigure design, with the most notable changes being switching black to earth blue and different leg printing that matches other Alpha Team agents in the subtheme. He wears a dark grey Mini Crash Helmet with a transparent blue Divers Mask and a dark grey Oxygenbottle With Tube, with his black Mini Headsquare Scarf supplied as an alternative hair piece.
entities.short_description: Crunch, also known as Tanxx in Germany and Сапер (Saper, "Sapper") in Russian, is an Alpha Team minifigure first introduced in a 2000 video game before making a physical debut in 2001.

entities.name: Dash Justice
entities.description:
Dash Justice, often simply called Dash, is an Alpha Team minifigure released physically in 2001 after debuting in 5714 LEGO Alpha Team in 2000.

In the video game and in the 2001 sets, Dash Justice wears an all-black jumpsuit which includes: several pockets, several lasers, the Alpha Team globe insignia, and a distinct button-up collar. His belt was blank, and his legs included pockets and two textured pads. His hair is an earth orange Mini Wig, Crewcut, with the physical piece being based directly upon the nonphysical hairpiece in the video game. Dash is the only Alpha Team agent to lack a colored right sleeve.

In the Mission Deep Sea subtheme, Dash wears nearly exact same jumpsuit, but in earth blue and with a different leg print. He has the standard "double-bar" colour scheme, with a triangular pattern running down the sides. He often wears a dark grey Oxygenbottle With Tube and Mini Crash Helmet with a transparent blue visor: the visor is typically a Divers Mask, but it is a Mini Visor 2 in 4789 AT Aquatic Mech. His face was slightly changed, giving him grey eyes and a cleft chin.

In the Mission Deep Freeze subtheme, Dash wears sunglasses and a completely different outfit. His right sleeve is now bright blue (Charge's previous colour), and his shirt pattern is simpler, showing only a newer, triangular insignia, and several silver lines on the sides of the torso. He wears a silver belt, and several silver lines run down his pant legs. Due to earth orange being retired in 2004, his hair colour has been updated to reddish brown. In several nonphysical sources (such as the Mission Deep Freeze homepage, the Red Lens online games, and the Brick Street Journal), Dash retains his original face design.
entities.short_description: Dash Justice, often simply called Dash, is an Alpha Team minifigure released physically in 2001 after debuting in 5714 LEGO Alpha Team in 2000.

entities.name: Diamond Tooth
entities.description:
Diamond Tooth, also known as simply Diamond, is an Alpha Team Mission Deep Freeze minifigure introduced in 2004.

Diamond Tooth wears a black Mini Pixie Cap and the black standard Mission Deep Freeze Alpha Team uniform with a dark green right sleeve. His face is printed with a frowning facial expression, a black goatee, black sunglasses, a dark grey bandana, and a silver microphone.

Diamond Tooth is Alpha Team's mining expert. He is one of the new agents recruited by Alpha Team for Mission Deep Freeze. As an Alpha-3 agent, he pilots the Tundra Tracker.

After Radia is frozen by Ogel to prevent her from revealing his evil plans, Diamond Tooth drives the Tundra Tracker to rescue her. Upon discovering her location, he uses the Magma Drill to unfreeze her and then disables a nearby Ice Orb.
entities.short_description: Diamond Tooth, also known as simply Diamond, is an Alpha Team Mission Deep Freeze minifigure introduced in 2004.

entities.name: Flex
entities.description:
Flex, also known as Migh in Germany and Aркан (Arkan, "Lasso") in Russia, is an Alpha Team minifigure first introduced in a 2000 video game before making a physical debut in 2001.

In 5714 LEGO Alpha Team, Flex wears the general black jumpsuit with an Alpha Team globe insignia on his left torso. He has an orange stripe from his right shoulder down to his right leg, matching his bright orange bright sleeve. He has ropes slung across his torso, from his right shoulder to his left hip, representing his expertise. On his belt, he has three grey capsules and two pouches. He also has two pockets on his thighs and a kneepad directly below. His gloves are grey. He wears a black Flying Helmet that is modified with extra textures and a ring for attaching rope to Flex's Helmet Dangler. His face bears a very large open-mouthed smile and a comm headset.

In 2001, Flex's physical minifigure very closely resembles his video game design, albeit with simpler details on the ropes and capsules as well as an unmodified Flying Helmet.

In Mission Deep Sea, Flex's minifigure wears an almost identical outfit, but in earth blue instead of black. Instead of rope, he now wears what appears to be a sort of industrial wire across his chest. As with other Alpha Team agents, his hip and leg printing has been updated to match the style of the Mission Deep Sea uniform, eschewing the pockets and kneepads in favor of orange and grey striping. His Flying Helmet has been replaced with a dark grey Mini Crash Helmet with a transparent blue Divers Mask and a dark grey Oxygenbottle With Tube. His face printing slightly shrinks his smile and gives him visible orange/silver hair, with bangs extending over his right eye.
entities.short_description: Flex, also known as Migh in Germany and Aркан (Arkan, "Lasso") in Russia, is an Alpha Team minifigure first introduced in a 2000 video game before making a physical debut in 2001.

entities.name: Ice Drone
entities.description:
The Ice Drone, also known as Ogel agent, Ogel Drone, and Ogel Minion, is an Alpha Team minifigure introduced in 2004.

The Ice Drone wears a uniform that is derived from the previous Skeleton Drone uniform, but with some notable differences. The torso, left arm, and left leg are black, while the rest of the uniform is dark red. The torso is printed with the shape of a scarab. The Ice Drone has a white Mini Head No. 190 skull and wears a transparent fluorescent blue Insect Helm.

Ice Drones are Skeleton Drones that appear exclusively in Mission Deep Freeze, acting as Ogel's minions in piloting Snow Crawlers and spreading Ice Orbs across the globe.

Compared to the stiff and emotionless Skeleton Drones in previous Alpha Team comics, these Ice Drones show some individual personality in their humorous dialogue. In LEGO Magazine issue 5.04, two Ice Drones spell out Vladek's name in a manner reminiscent of cheerleaders, and one Ice Drone empathizes with Ogel's disappointment that Cool Creations are not used to take over the world. In the Adventures mini-comic in LEGO Magazine September/October 2005, Ogel berates his Ice Drones for leaving an Ice Orb in Morcia.
entities.short_description: The Ice Drone, also known as Ogel agent, Ogel Drone, and Ogel Minion, is an Alpha Team minifigure introduced in 2004.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. LEGO art © The LEGO Group (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Ogel
entities.description:
Ogel, often referred to with the title Evil Ogel and occasionally stylized as OGEL, is the villain of the Alpha Team theme.

The original 5714 LEGO Alpha Team video game design of Ogel has a plain black torso/arms and legs, a custom armor piece, and a black helmet with a large gold visor. His face is never revealed. The color of his hands is inconsistent, with his in-game appearances in LEGO Alpha Team having yellow hands, but the intro animation for LEGO Logic giving him black hands. The final intro for the LEGO Alpha Team game shows him with both yellow and black hands at different points. This design is also used in Evil Music with yellow hands.

When LEGO released sets based on LEGO Alpha Team in 2001, Ogel's design was tweaked. He is given a slightly modified version of Alien, Breast Plate, as the original version of the piece does not allow his Mini Crash Helmet to fit properly. His helmet's visor is represented with a metalized gold Space Visor. His hands are now consistently black, and his face is revealed (which partially recycles Señor Palomar's face design, but with a different mouth and slightly higher placed eyes, one of which is red). It is unknown if Ogel's face was designed by the game developers and just never shown by them, or if LEGO designed the face themselves when it came time to produce physical sets.

In the Alpha Team Stunt Show, Ogel wears a black outfit with red chest and shoulderpads reminiscent of his video game armor, a red belt, and red stripes on his right leg. At some point during the show, Ogel wears a blonde wig with feminine pigtails.
entities.short_description: Ogel, often referred to with the title Evil Ogel and occasionally stylized as OGEL, is the villain of the Alpha Team theme.

entities.name: Radia
entities.description:
Radia is an Alpha Team minifigure released in 2001 after making her video game debut in 2000.

In the 5714 LEGO Alpha Team PC game, Radia wears a black jumpsuit, with the left side of her torso being colored white and the right side of her torso being colored violet. Her right sleeve is bright violet, and her gloves are grey. Her legs featured pockets and two textured kneepads. She has a white Mini U.S. Cap textured with the Alpha Team logo, and two modeled violet pigtails. Her face is printed with red lipstick, violet eyeliner, violet hair, and a headset with a microphone.

On the box art for LEGO Alpha Team, the black portions of Radia's torso (including her left sleeve) are colored white instead. The title screen of the 5725 LEGO Alpha Team GBC version and the cover of the instruction manual are based upon an older render of Radia, which depicted her with a black shirt, light pink instead of violet, different tools on her belt, no eyeliner, and no logo on her hat. Likely due to being a remnant of this, Radia's uniform color is listed as white instead of purple on the LEGO Alpha Team website.

When Radia made her physical debut in 2001, her minifigure design was based upon her video game model with some changes. Her torso print was given greater detail, including the Alpha Team logo and what appears to be black drawstrings, although one piece of equipment on her belt was changed to a pouch. Her hip also features a bit of violet printing on the right side to continue the pattern from her torso to her leg. However, her right sleeve has been changed from violet to black, her hat no longer sports the Alpha Team logo, and her pigtails have been removed.
entities.short_description: Radia is an Alpha Team minifigure released in 2001 after making her video game debut in 2000.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. LEGO art © The LEGO Group (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Skeleton Drone
entities.description:
Skeleton Drones, also known as Zombies and Skeleton Zombies, are Alpha Team minifigures first introduced in a 2000 video game before making a physical debut in 2001.

True to their name, Skeleton Drones have white skull faces and are dressed in red and black uniforms in every variant.

In the original video game 5714 LEGO Alpha Team released in 2000, on which the theme was based, Zombies have a custom head print with hypnotized eyes and a wide toothy grin. However, some in-game images (such as large posters in Ogel's bases) and the intro cutscene of the Game Boy Color version show them with normal skeleton heads.

Guards, Troopers, and Lurchers wear uniforms that are red on the right side and black on the left side, a silver belt going across their lower torso, and a black Mini Cap. Guards and Troopers have red epaulets and gloves, but Lurchers have black gloves and no epaulets.
entities.short_description: Skeleton Drones, also known as Zombies and Skeleton Zombies, are Alpha Team minifigures first introduced in a 2000 video game before making a physical debut in 2001.

entities.name: Super Ice Drone
entities.description:
The Super Ice Drone is an Alpha Team minifigure introduced in 2005.

The Super Ice Drone's design is derived from the standard Ice Drone, but with some notable differences. The torso, left arm, and left leg are black, while the rest of the uniform is dark red. The torso is printed with the shape of a scarab; unlike normal Ice Drones, this scarab has a white outline. The Super Ice Drone has a unique black "evil" skull with white outlines and glowing red eyes, and wears a transparent fluorescent blue Insect Helm.

The Super Ice Drone is a special type of Ice Drone that pilots the Scorpion Orb Launcher, which is pursued by Flex and his ice glider. Little else is known about the Super Ice Drone, since it does not appear in the theme's storyline in any capacity; the LEGO Magazine comics instead depict Ogel piloting the Scorpion Orb Launcher during the final battle.

entities.name: Tee Vee
entities.description:
Tee Vee, alternatively formatted as Tee-Vee or TeeVee and also known as AT-1 in Germany, is an Alpha Team minifigure, first introduced the 2000 video game 5714 LEGO Alpha Team before appearing as a physical minifigure in 2001.

In LEGO Alpha Team, Tee Vee is portrayed as a white television (represented by a printed 1x2 brick) mounted on white minifigure legs with a black hip piece, along with black antennae and a transparent blue light bulb mounted next to the screen. His physical minifigure in 6775 Alpha Team Bomb Squad was nearly identical to his appearance in LEGO Alpha Team, but with the electric light bulb cover (part 4773) replaced with a 1x1 round plate in the same color.

In 2002, Tee Vee appears as a brick-built ROV instead of a minifigure. The ROV has a bright yellow and black colour scheme, and appears with two slight variants between 4792 Alpha Team Navigator and ROV and 4789 AT Aquatic Mech, with the latter being slightly smaller and more compact than the former.

When Alpha Team was relaunched in 2004, Tee Vee was shown to have a new android body.

entities.name: Zed
entities.description:
Zed is an Alpha Team Mission Deep Freeze minifigure introduced in 2005.

Zed wears a black snowsuit with silver printed lines, multiple silver straps with small blue buttons, and a unique elliptical insignia on the chest; aside from the insignia, this is a color variant of Flex and Charge's uniforms. Unlike other Mission Deep Freeze minifigures, both of his arms and hands are bright yellow. His face bears a confident smirk, a blue soul patch, and blue/black gradient hair with a yellow checkerboard pattern on the right side.

In his brief cameo in Prehistoric Creatures Vs. Team Titan XP, Zed's torso is bright yellow.

Zed is an Alpha Team special agent. At the end of Prehistoric Creatures Vs. Team Titan XP, Zed is on a warm and sunny beach when he receives Dash Justice's emergency beacon. He pilots the Blizzard Blaster, which is equipped with special time tech to protect it from Ogel's time freeze wave. He arrives at Ogel's Mountain Fortress and uses a thermo ray to melt the ice and rescue his fellow Alpha Team agents. He battles Ogel's Scorpion Orb Launcher.
entities.short_description: Zed is an Alpha Team Mission Deep Freeze minifigure introduced in 2005.

entities.name: Blathers
entities.description: The life simulation video game series Animal Crossing, created by Katsuya Eguchi and first released in 2001 by Nintendo, features an assortment of recurring characters. Titles in the series follow the player character as they live in a village populated by anthropomorphic animals, with gameplay that proceeds in a nonlinear fashion and in-game events that occur in real-time. As of Animal Crossing: New Horizons, the most recent release in the series, there are over 400 animal characters that can potentially populate a player's village. In addition to these villager characters, Animal Crossing features characters that appear in the villages of all players; these characters typically serve a particular gameplay function, or appear at a specific in-game event.

entities.name: Bunnie
entities.description:
Rabbits, or bunnies, are small mammals in the family Leporidae (which also includes the hares), which is in the order Lagomorpha (which also includes pikas). They are familiar throughout the world as a small herbivore, a prey animal, a domesticated form of livestock, and a pet, having a widespread effect on ecologies and cultures. The most widespread rabbit genera are Oryctolagus and Sylvilagus. The former, Oryctolagus, includes the European rabbit, Oryctolagus cuniculus, which is the ancestor of the hundreds of breeds of domestic rabbit and has been introduced on every continent except Antarctica. The latter, Sylvilagus, includes over 13 wild rabbit species, among them the cottontails and tapetis. Wild rabbits not included in Oryctolagus and Sylvilagus include several species of limited distribution, including the pygmy rabbit, volcano rabbit, and Sumatran striped rabbit.

Rabbits are a paraphyletic grouping, and do not constitute a clade, as hares (belonging to the genus Lepus) are nested within the Leporidae clade and are not described as rabbits. Although once considered rodents, lagomorphs diverged earlier and have a number of traits rodents lack, including two extra incisors. Similarities between rabbits and rodents were once attributed to convergent evolution, but studies in molecular biology have found a common ancestor between lagomorphs and rodents and place them in the clade Glires.

Rabbit physiology is suited to escaping predators and surviving in various habitats, living either alone or in groups in nests or burrows. As prey animals, rabbits are constantly aware of their surroundings, having a wide field of vision and ears with high surface area to detect potential predators. The ears of a rabbit are essential for thermoregulation and contain a high density of blood vessels. The bone structure of a rabbit's hind legs, which is longer than that of the fore legs, allows for quick hopping, which is beneficial for escaping predators and can provide powerful kicks if captured. Rabbits are typically nocturnal and often sleep with their eyes open. They reproduce quickly, having short pregnancies, large litters of four to twelve kits, and no particular mating season; however, the mortality rate of rabbit embryos is high, and there exist several widespread diseases that affect rabbits, such as rabbit hemorrhagic disease and myxomatosis. In some regions, especially Australia, rabbits have caused ecological problems and are regarded as a pest.

Humans have used rabbits as livestock since at least the first century BC in ancient Rome, raising them for their meat, fur and wool. The various breeds of the European rabbit have been developed to suit each of these products; the practice of raising and breeding rabbits as livestock is known as cuniculture. Rabbits are seen in human culture globally, appearing as a symbol of fertility, cunning, and innocence in major religions, historical and contemporary art.

entities.name: Fauna
entities.description: Fauna (pl.: faunae or faunas) is all the animal life present in a particular region or time. The corresponding terms for plants and fungi are flora and funga, respectively. Flora, fauna, funga and other forms of life are collectively referred to as biota. Zoologists and paleontologists use fauna to refer to a typical collection of animals found in a specific time or place, e.g. the "Sonoran Desert fauna" or the "Burgess Shale fauna". Paleontologists sometimes refer to a sequence of faunal stages, which is a series of rocks all containing similar fossils. The study of animals of a particular region is called faunistics.

entities.name: Maple
entities.description: Acer is a genus of trees and shrubs commonly known as maples. The genus is placed in the soapberry family Sapindaceae. There are approximately 132 species, most of which are native to East Asia, with a number also appearing in Europe, northern Africa, and North America. Only one species, Acer laurinum, extends to the Southern Hemisphere. The type species of the genus is the sycamore maple Acer pseudoplatanus, one of the most common maple species in Europe. Most maples have easily identifiable palmate leaves (with a few exceptions, such as Acer carpinifolium, Acer laurinum, and Acer negundo) and all share distinctive winged fruits. The closest relative of the maples is the small east Asian genus Dipteronia, followed by the more widespread genus Aesculus (buckeyes and horse-chestnuts). Maple syrup is made from the sap of some maple species. It is one of the most common genera of trees in Asia. Many maple species are grown in gardens where they are valued for their autumn colour and often decorative foliage, some also for their attractive flowers, fruit, or bark.

entities.name: Stitches
entities.description:
A surgical suture, also known as a stitch or stitches, is a medical device used to hold body tissues together and approximate wound edges after an injury or surgery. Application generally involves using a needle with an attached length of thread. There are numerous types of suture which differ by needle shape and size as well as thread material and characteristics. Selection of surgical suture should be determined by the characteristics and location of the wound or the specific body tissues being approximated.

In selecting the needle, thread, and suturing technique to use for a specific patient, a medical care provider must consider the tensile strength of the specific suture thread needed to efficiently hold the tissues together depending on the mechanical and shear forces acting on the wound as well as the thickness of the tissue being approximated. One must also consider the elasticity of the thread and ability to adapt to different tissues, as well as the memory of the thread material which lends to ease of use for the operator. Different suture characteristics lend way to differing degrees of tissue reaction and the operator must select a suture that minimizes the tissue reaction while still keeping with appropriate tensile strength.
